ABSTRACTThis article examines whether realized extreme drought episodes affect the speed of adjustment of derived input demands and output supplies toward their long‐run equilibrium in U.S. agriculture, focusing on states in the North Central Region. Using state‐level data from 1960 to 2015, we estimate a dynamic investment‐demand and output‐supply system based on adjustment cost theory.

Efficient irrigation is pivotal for viticulture in arid regions; however, solutions that simultaneously stabilize vine water status, sustain yield, and preserve fruit quality remain limited. We evaluated a microfiber-based wicking infiltration irrigation system—applied at the surface (W1) and shallow-buried at 10 cm (W2)—against drip (DI) and furrow (FI) irrigation in a two-year field trial with table grapes in northwest China. Additional wicking infiltration irrigation quota treatments (W1-2/3, W1-1/3) were also tested.

Irrigation management is essential for successfully cultivating Chile peppers (Capsicum spp.), as it influences plant yield, fruit quality, and susceptibility to soil-borne diseases. This study investigates the effects of various sprinkler irrigation regimes on different Chile pepper varieties to optimize water use efficiency and enhance overall production. The varieties included in the study are ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’, ‘Anaheim’, ‘Sandia’, ‘NM#6’, ‘California Wonder’, and ‘Red Knight’.

From a ‘globalist’ new world order to the alleged ‘replacement’ of national populations through ‘dangerous alien Others’, conspiracy theories about global politics are thriving and increasingly entering the mainstream discourse. This paper analyses the ideological force, functions and effects of far-right conspiracy theories. Drawing on Lacanian Ontological Security Studies, it relates conspiracy theories to the ontological lack around which our identities and social orders are constituted.

abstract: Since the turn of the millennium, the field of global labor history has seen a flood of publications and the establishment of associations worldwide, contributing significantly to the renewal of labor history and history in general. After a brief introduction to global labor history, this article discusses some of its key issues, particularly the relationship between labor regulation and historical labor dynamics. These discussions critically evaluate the conceptual and historical tensions between free and unfree labor.

With the continuous rise in global temperatures, particularly within arid regions, maintaining thermal comfort in naturally ventilated buildings presents a significant challenge. This study investigates the effectiveness of biomaterial-infused bricks in mitigating indoor overheating in low-income residential buildings. The findings indicate that all tested bio-brick families contribute to a notable reduction in unmet thermal comfort hours compared with conventional clay bricks.

This review examines additive manufacturing (AM) of nuclear materials. Three core advantages of AM for nuclear reactor components are identified: high geometric complexity, short lead times, and tunable microstructures. Five mainstream AM technologies are reviewed: laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), directed energy deposition (DED), electron beam powder bed fusion (EB-PBF), wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), and binder jetting.

This study addresses the environmental sustainability of making fired clay bricks using Waste Marble Powder (WMP) and Sugarcane Bagasse Ash (SBA) to substitute up to 50 percent of virgin clay. The physical, mechanical, and durability properties of experimental batches with different WMP and SBA content (0-30%) were compared based on the ASTM standards. The studies found an ideal combination of 10% WMP and 5% SBA that had a compressive strength of more than 8 MPa, which was a structural requirement.

AbstractSoils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0–90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure.

This interdisciplinary narrative review integrates findings from nutritional science, climate adaptation studies, recent genomic innovations, and policy analyses (2010–2025) to critically evaluate dairy goats’ roles in addressing persistent malnutrition and vulnerability to climate extremes. Selecting a reinforced concrete construction system is usually justified either economically or environmentally, and the two perspectives are rarely derived from the same project data. It therefore remains unclear whether the cost-optimal and the carbon-optimal choice coincide, and whether the differences between the systems are large enough to be distinguished from the uncertainty of the underlying assumptions. This study addresses that question for a real industrial building in northern Germany.

Global warming has made climate physical and transition risks systemic sources of financial instability and key challenges to sustainability. These risks can spread to carbon, energy, and metals markets, which are central to the low-carbon transition and sustainable finance. This paper, therefore, explores the Quantile Time-Frequency connections among climate physical risk, climate transition risk, and the carbon, energy, and metals markets, with the analysis conducted through the lens of higher-moment risks.

Poverty eradication remains a central challenge for sustainable development, yet its environmental determinants are not sufficiently explored. Theoretically, air pollution may exacerbate poverty. However, empirical research on how air pollution influences global poverty is lacking.

Climate change mitigation increasingly hinges on decarbonising the built environment, yet renewable energy integration in building construction remains underexplored in many emerging economies in Africa, including Ghana. This study examined the enhanced deployment of renewable energy sources (RES) in real estate projects as a contribution to climate change mitigation using the IDT approach. Using quantitative design methodologies, data was collected from 400 professionals working in the real estate industry, receiving a response rate of 94 %.

Abiotic stresses reduce barley growth and yield by elevating the free radicals such as reactive oxygen (ROS), nitrogen (RNS), carbonyl (RCS), and sulfur species (RSS) in plant cells. Among these, hydrogen sulfide (H2S), classified as RSS, serves as a signalling molecule and growth regulator in stress responses. However, the optimal sodium hydrosulphide (NaHS; an H2S donor) concentrations for barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) remain unknown.

The methods used in monitoring the increasing drought are vitally significant. In order to determine and monitor drought, many scientific studies have been carried out in our country, especially using the standardized precipitation index (SPI). However, due to increasing temperatures and evaporation, there is a need for studies showing the spatio-temporal change of drought at the country scale according to the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI), which also takes evaporation into account.

An improved biogeography-based optimization (IBBO) algorithm is proposed for determining the optimal parameter values of a multi-partition nonlinear Muskingum flood routing model. The evaluation was conducted for two model structures, namely, the three-partition (3P) and five-partition (5P) configurations, using three benchmark datasets: Wilson, Wyre River, and Viessman–Lewis.

ABSTRACTThe gut virome is a critical component of the microbiome-gut-brain axis; however, its role in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) remains poorly understood due to limited sample sizes and geographic bias. We aimed to construct a comprehensive global atlas of the IBS gut virome to elucidate its composition, functional potential, and clinical relevance across diverse populations and IBS subtypes. We integrated multi-cohort data comprising 1,104 samples (790 IBS patients and 314 healthy controls) from 11 cohorts across 10 geographic regions.
